correctness.rationale: The source gives, for every width \(0<\delta\le1/20\), a globally smooth tube function constant outside its tube, bounded below by \(f_\infty-2\delta\), with Hessian norm at most \(K/\delta^2\), and an affine ratio map satisfying \(r(1)<6\delta\) and \(r(0)>1-6\delta\). Choosing \(\delta(q)=\min\{1/20,q/12,(1-q)/12\}\) therefore realizes every target \(q\in(0,1)\). Spatial scaling by \(b=1/\delta\) converts the Hessian bound to \(K\) and the unit orbit gradient to the positive constant \(\delta\), while preserving normalized decrease ratios, exact endpoint orthogonality, and conjugacy rays. The source polyline has summable transverse heading error, so each scaled tube lies in a finite-width strip; recursive transverse translations make the strips pairwise disjoint and locally finite. The resulting sum is \(C^\infty\), bounded below, and has uniformly bounded Hessian. Rational density covers every Goldstein interval. The common-start impossibility follows because a fixed first-local-minimizer step has one fixed normalized decrease ratio that cannot belong to every subinterval of \((0,1)\).

value.rationale: The primary paper explicitly identifies parameter-universalization as an open structural question. The finding gives a single globally smooth lower-bounded Lipschitz-gradient objective covering every line-search parameter pair when starts may vary, while keeping one uniform Hessian bound despite the source family's \(1/\delta^2\) blow-up. It also proves that the stronger common-start interpretation is impossible under simultaneous Goldstein validity. This separates the real mathematical issue from an ambiguity in the quantifiers and turns a family of parameter-specific counterexamples into one universal objective without weakening the line-search conditions.
